checks: Checked 58f3f048f8ef3f61:01 §1 (1)–(5). At tilt −b the negative extreme is inside supporting and the positive extreme is outside supporting. Decreasing the tilt makes those traces strict with no change in their masses, while the three middle traces stay proper.
The derivative along the decreasing-tilt direction is r_−1−r_1, since the two contributing intermediate bases are −1 and 1. Local optimality forces this difference nonnegative.

For finite A>max_z(H_z+δ), every negative non-own base is empty and each positive base is full, with unchanged own trace. Subtracting the two exact integrated masses gives the half base first moment minus b times the width difference and δ times their sum.

The continuous means vanish for centered rectangles, so full balance makes the half base moment zero. Positive δ gives strict improvement; at δ=0 global minimality forces equal widths, and the small decreased tilt then has exactly constant mass and strict endpoint traces.

The lower-dimensional supporting example uses a different contact pattern and a displaced mark. It does not impose the centered full mixed centroid condition here.
